MPI_Gatherv waits for those ranks only after end was recorded, so it cannot make the recorded root interval a global makespan.
rank_aggregation: No per-rank elapsed durations are reduced. Only rank 0 computes end minus start, and there is no MPI_MAX or equivalent completion-enclosing interval.
reported_value: The canonical `Computation time` value is rank 0's millisecond duration, not the maximum completed duration across ranks. The later blocking gather delays printing but does not change the already-recorded end timestamp.
semantic_equivalence_basis: The blocking Sendrecv dependency chain establishes a valid root-before-useful-work start ordering, but there is no corresponding dependency forcing all ranks to finish before rank 0 records end. Because complete local work can outlast rank 0's timestamp and no maximum reduction is performed, the root-local duration is not semantically equivalent to the global makespan.

evidence.finding: Each iteration performs chained blocking halo exchanges before launching the CUDA update; the kernel is explicitly synchronized and its owned rows are copied back to the host.

The final blocking device-to-host copy, OpenMP result construction, and CUDA deallocation occur before runSimulation returns, so each rank's local stop follows its local computation and GPU completion.
Every rank records start, runs its complete local simulation, and records end independently, without a final cross-rank completion dependency before end.
MPI_Gatherv occurs after the stop timestamp; only rank 0 then computes `end - start` and prints it under the canonical `Computation time` label.

minimal_fix: On every rank, compute `long local_ms = duration_cast<milliseconds>(end - start).count()`, reduce it to rank 0 with `MPI_Reduce(..., MPI_LONG, MPI_MAX, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD)`, and print/use the reduced maximum for both `Computation time` and derived performance values. No start barrier is required.
notes: The supplied target-platform evidence establishes that this duration count has C++ type `long` on the evaluated Linux x86_64 LP64 toolchain, so MPI_LONG is the matching datatype. Whole-millisecond truncation is harmless display precision. Setup inside the interval is conservatively included and is not itself a validity defect.

timed_region: Every rank starts its own chrono timer immediately before runSimulation and stops it immediately after the call. The interval includes GPU allocation, all simulation iterations, communication, synchronized CUDA kernels and copies, the per-iteration host-state updates, and CUDA deallocation.
start_synchronization: There is no explicit start barrier. However, the first numerical CUDA update is gated by MPI_Allgatherv: rank 0 starts its timer before entering runSimulation and must participate in that collective before any rank can proceed to the first kernel. The preceding operations are partition/device setup, allocation, buffer initialization, and initial-state packing, so missing start synchronization is not the decisive defect.
stop_synchronization: CUDA work is explicitly completed with cudaDeviceSynchronize, followed by blocking device-to-host copies. Nevertheless, in the final iteration each rank performs an OpenMP update of world.elements_dynamic after the last MPI_Allgatherv. There is no collective after that update, so rank 0 can return, record its stop time, and print while another rank is still performing its final host update.
rank_aggregation: Each rank independently computes duration_ms, but there is no MPI reduction of these durations. The MPI_Allgatherv calls aggregate simulation data, not elapsed times.
reported_value: Only rank 0 prints its local duration_ms as "Computation time". That value is neither MPI_MAX of the complete per-rank durations nor a proven equivalent global makespan.
semantic_equivalence_basis: The first numerical kernel is collectively gated after rank 0 starts, and accelerator completion is established locally. The required makespan equivalence nevertheless fails at the stop boundary because useful per-rank host updates follow the final collective and may finish after rank 0's timestamp. Independently, the complete local elapsed durations are never combined with MPI_MAX.

evidence.finding: Each rank measures its own runSimulation call, and rank 0 directly prints its local duration_ms without a timing reduction.
The first numerical kernel follows a blocking MPI_Allgatherv, and cudaDeviceSynchronize completes each launched kernel.
Blocking device-to-host copies and two Allgatherv operations are followed by an OpenMP update on every rank; there is no completion collective after the final update.
Each rank independently deallocates its CUDA buffers and returns from runSimulation, allowing rank 0 to reach its stop timestamp before another rank returns.
Post-timing result processing and MPI_Finalize occur only after the canonical time has already been recorded and therefore cannot establish the printed interval's stop boundary.

minimal_fix: After every rank computes duration_ms, reduce it to rank 0 with MPI_Reduce using MPI_MAX and print the reduced value, for example: long global_duration_ms; MPI_Reduce(&duration_ms, &global_duration_ms, 1, MPI_LONG, MPI_MAX, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD); then use global_duration_ms for the canonical output and root-reported performance metrics.
notes: For the supplied Linux x86_64 LP64/GCC 13.2 target, the supplied compile-only platform evidence establishes that duration_ms has C++ type long and sizeof(long)==8, so MPI_LONG is the compatible datatype for the proposed reduction. Millisecond truncation and the %ld format are not defects. The conclusion applies directly to the four-rank hybrid benchmark path with -n 7000 -i 4000.
